## Pressure accuracy at the selected states

{{< include figures/outcome.md >}}

This is a **fixed-parameter comparison; historical calibration overlap unresolved**.
The result is a coupled-pressure test, predominantly of neutral-mixture behavior in this range.
It does not test speciation and does not support physical validation beyond these three states.
It does not establish a within-uncertainty pressure claim even for these states.
No measured pH, dissociation fraction or ionic activity is compared.
A stronger speciation test requires independent activity or dissociation measurements.

## Question, basis and fixed declaration

How accurately does the declared native reacting bubble calculation reproduce the selected measured total pressures, without fitting its parameters to those measurements?
The source identities, exact locators, activity conventions and acquisition limits are retained in [source notes](inputs/source-notes.md), [parameters](inputs/parameters.json), [reactions and numerical criteria](inputs/reactions.json), and [measurement lineage](inputs/measurement-lineage.json).

{{< include figures/conditions.md >}}

The liquid contains water, molecular acetic acid, formal hydrogen ions, acetate and hydroxide.
The incipient vapor contains only water and molecular acid and has zero pinned amount.
The Engine solves pressure, phase densities, liquid reaction equilibrium, charge conservation and neutral-species vapor–liquid fugacity equality together.
The declared reactions and source activity quotients are

$$
\mathrm{HAc \rightleftharpoons H^+ + Ac^-},
\qquad K_{a,m}=\frac{a_{H^+}a_{Ac^-}}{a_{HAc}},
$$

$$
\mathrm{H_2O \rightleftharpoons H^+ + OH^-},
\qquad K_w=\frac{a_{H^+}a_{OH^-}}{a_w}.
$$

Solute activities use the common molality infinite-dilution standard in pure water; water uses its pure-liquid standard.
The IAPWS hydronium convention is converted explicitly to the formal hydrogen-ion convention in the retained source declaration.
Source pressures remain fixed while the Engine transfers the standards to the solved state.
The acid's adopted reference pressure is not a measurement of its pressure dependence.

The equation of state uses hard-chain, dispersion, association, Debye–Hückel and uncorrected Born terms.
The adopted water/acid/ion family excludes like-sign ion dispersion and uses the published water–acid binary interaction with zero temperature coefficient.
Both neutral species have one donor and one acceptor site.
Gross–Sadowski cross-association includes the segment-size factor, an explicit interpretation where Ascani's supplement does not state a cross rule.
Component-permittivity mixing includes both water and acid with salt-free solvent mass fractions and the total solvent mole fraction, plus the ionic permittivity contribution.
The original declaration, with only water assigned a neutral dielectric record, remains a control.
The published parameters remain fixed throughout the comparison.

## Measurements and inherited calibration

The retained NIST ThermoML record of Bernatová–Aim–Wichterle joins pressure group 13 and liquid-water-composition group 14 by their common reported gas-water mole fraction.
The gas fraction is not the liquid feed composition.
The extraction retains every joined row and marks the acid-rich rows excluded from this owner-selected comparison.
Pure-component endpoints are not counted as reacting-mixture observations.
Molecular partial-pressure scoring is excluded because the chemically corrected vapor-composition convention has not been reconciled with true-species molecular vapor.

The stated uncertainties are combined expanded uncertainties at the compiler's reported confidence level, not standard deviations or independently verified author uncertainty estimates.
The record supplies neither a temperature uncertainty nor a joint input/output covariance for this selection.

Gross–Sadowski pure-component saturation and density fitting and the adopted water/ion parameter family are inherited calibration.
Ascani's later binary-parameter table traces the water–acid interaction to Pabsch's binary vapor–liquid fitting.
The recovered Pabsch supplement identifies the binary fit source and printed temperature interval, as discussed below.
The individual fitted rows and complete original model declaration remain unavailable.
Membership of the Bernatová observations in that historical fit is therefore **unresolved**.
There is no local calibration set, independent withheld-prediction claim, or claim to replay the exact historically fitted model.

Signed error means calculated minus measured pressure.
The root-mean-square error uses the signed pressure errors before squaring; relative errors divide by the measured pressure.
Numerical failures are counted separately and are never silently omitted from a score.

## Controls and the speciation limit

{{< include figures/controls.md >}}

Each control changes only the named declaration on the same installed wheel.
The no-dissociation control removes both reactions and ions while retaining the neutral molecular parameters.
The acid-only control retains acid dissociation and omits water ionization; its maximum pressure difference is below the numerical resolution of this comparison.
Water ionization remains included in the primary declaration.
The acid-permittivity control compares the sourced two-solvent declaration with the original water-only dielectric declaration, keeping the reaction declarations fixed.

{{< include figures/speciation-limit.md >}}

The sourced acid permittivity reduces that signal further.
The pressure measurement cannot distinguish the reported speciation at this resolution.
The computed liquid dissociation fractions in the raw state table are model outputs, not validated measurements.
Permittivity, ionic-parameter and single-ion-activity accuracy remain unvalidated.

## Input-interval falsifier

For each state, define the conditional calculated interval $I_{\mathrm{calc}}$ from the retained composition sweep and numerical expansion, and the measured interval $I_{\mathrm{meas}}=[P-U_P,P+U_P]$.
If $I_{\mathrm{calc}}\cap I_{\mathrm{meas}}=\varnothing$, that state falsifies the declared within-interval pressure claim.
One disjoint state falsifies a claim covering all selected states.
Overlap would mean only that this test did not falsify the claim.

{{< include figures/uncertainty.md >}}

The retained pressures increase across each input interval and the exact native pressure derivatives are positive at every sampled state.
This supplies numerical evidence for the smooth monotone branch used to select the endpoint ranges.
Finite samples do not prove the absence of an unsampled turning point; these are numerically qualified conditional ranges, not certified interval arithmetic.
No joint confidence region, model confidence interval or probability of failure is inferred from the Cartesian input/output intervals.
The temperature and adopted parameters are fixed; their missing uncertainty budgets remain unknown, not zero.
The observed separation therefore supports a conditional discrepancy under this declaration, not an uncertainty-complete rejection of every possible parameterization.

## Why the calculated bubble pressure is too high

The positive pressure error lies in the neutral binary mixture's departure from
its pure-component pressure endpoints.
Both pure-component pressures have negative central errors, so their endpoint
contributions partly mask the positive mixture departure.
This excludes an explanation through excessive pure-component endpoint pressures
with the mixture departure held fixed.
Pure-component dispersion and association parameters also affect mixture
nonideality; their contribution through that path remains unresolved.
Dissociation reduces pressure slightly and cannot explain the excess.

### Exact decomposition about the pure endpoints

Let $x$ denote the analytical liquid water mole fraction, $P_n$ the neutral
bubble pressure and $P_r$ the reacting bubble pressure.
Let $p_w^*$ and $p_a^*$ denote pure water and pure acetic-acid saturation
pressures; superscripts $m$ and $e$ denote model and measured values.
Define departure from the straight line between the pure endpoints by

$$
C^m(x)=P_n(x)-[x p_w^{*,m}+(1-x)p_a^{*,m}],
\qquad
C^e(x)=P^e(x)-[x p_w^{*,e}+(1-x)p_a^{*,e}].
$$

Adding and subtracting those endpoint lines gives the exact identity

$$
P_r-P^e=
\underbrace{x(p_w^{*,m}-p_w^{*,e})}_{\text{water endpoint}}+
\underbrace{(1-x)(p_a^{*,m}-p_a^{*,e})}_{\text{acid endpoint}}+
\underbrace{C^m-C^e}_{\text{mixing}}+
\underbrace{P_r-P_n}_{\text{dissociation}}.
$$

“Mixing” here means the difference between departures from the two endpoint
straight lines.
It includes both phases' nonideality and their equilibrium coupling, without
assuming an ideal vapour or Raoult's law.
It does not uniquely separate molecular interactions or measure a liquid excess
property.
The weights use analytical liquid composition, not the gas-composition join key.

{{< include results/pressure-diagnosis/decomposition-table.md >}}

The [complete decomposition](results/pressure-diagnosis/pressure-decomposition.csv)
retains all measured mixed compositions.
The error changes sign on the acid-rich side; it is not a uniform pressure multiplier.
Replacing only the model endpoints with measured values while holding the model
departure fixed increases the positive error, as the last column below shows.
That column is an arithmetic diagnostic, not a new equilibrium calculation.

{{< include results/pressure-diagnosis/departure-table.md >}}

### Pure-component comparison

The pure controls retain the mixture's pure coefficients, water diameter law
and association schemes and solve liquid–vapour coexistence natively.
The measured endpoints come from Bernatová–Aim–Wichterle's retained
[ThermoML record](inputs/bernatova-2006.json), pressure group 13 at the pure gas-water endpoints.

{{< include results/pressure-diagnosis/endpoints-table.md >}}

The uncertainties are compiler-evaluated combined expanded uncertainties at
95% confidence.
Water is inside its reported interval; its negative central error alone does
not establish a statistically resolved water-pressure bias.
Acid is below the central measurement and its stated interval.
Both central endpoint errors oppose the positive mixture error.

{{< include results/pressure-diagnosis/source-comparison.md >}}

The acid coefficients trace to [Gross–Sadowski (2002), Table 1](https://doi.org/10.1021/ie010954d),
which fits pure saturation pressure and liquid density together.
Its mean pressure deviation is not a pointwise uncertainty.
The [source notes](inputs/source-notes.md#diagnostic-sources-and-locators)
retain the coefficient and combining-rule locators.
The source-rounding control changes pressure only slightly.
Substituting the inconsistent acid dispersion energy printed in Ascani's later
table instead severely underpredicts pure-acid pressure; that substitution
is not a defensible correction.

### Binary interaction and association evidence

{{< include results/pressure-diagnosis/fit-conditions.md >}}

The [retained supplement text](inputs/source/pabsch-2022-si.txt),
[original supplement](inputs/source/pabsch-2022-si.docx) and
[Figure S1 extract](inputs/source/pabsch-figure-S1.png) preserve those locators.
The printed interval and plotted range remain distinct: the supplement does
not inventory individual fitted observations or establish that every fitted
row had the plotted pressure.
The original Ito–Yoshida observations and Pabsch's complete parameter and
association declaration were not recovered.
The binary fit cannot be inferred from the esterification experiment's temperature.

The following neutral bubble-pressure probes change one declaration at a time.
Their changes are relative to the unmodified neutral bubble pressure.
They are parameter sensitivities, without selecting a corrected parameter.

{{< include results/pressure-diagnosis/sensitivities-table.md >}}

Stronger unlike dispersion attraction reduces the calculated pressures by
hundreds of pascals.
That response establishes direction and scale, without identifying an erroneous
coefficient, a temperature law or a physical cause.
An effective dispersion interaction may compensate for limitations in association.
The printed square versus Gross–Sadowski's cube in the association volume size
factor accounts for only a small fraction of the discrepancy.
Even removing the size factor does not eliminate it.

Both water and acid use the classical 2B scheme: one donor and one acceptor,
with self association and both unlike donor–acceptor orientations.
The [association mass-action and Helmholtz equations](../../engine/docs/equations.md)
are evaluated at each phase's own density and composition.
Ordinary vapour association is present:

{{< include results/pressure-diagnosis/vapour-table.md >}}

Direct controls remove specified interactions at the same returned vapour
density and composition.
The self-removal control first writes the original cross strengths explicitly,
so removing self association does not also alter cross association.

{{< include results/pressure-diagnosis/same-state-table.md >}}

These direct state-pressure changes are not re-equilibrated bubble-pressure
changes or bounds on a different association theory.
The classical scheme contains no separate doubly bonded cyclic-dimer
contribution, dimer species or dimer reaction.
Unbonded-site fractions are not measured monomer or cyclic-dimer fractions.
[Janeček–Paricaud (2013), primary abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23806104/)
supports competition between cyclic dimers and cross association in acid mixtures
with water and alcohols, with improvements particularly in dew curves.
Only the abstract was inspected; its full equations and parameters were not tested.
It does not determine a correction's sign or magnitude for these bubble pressures.

### Ranked hypotheses and evidence needed for correction

The ranking gives investigation priority, not a measured causal ordering.

| Rank | Hypothesis | Evidence and limit |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Effective water–acid interaction transfers poorly to this colder isotherm under the adopted association model | The recovered binary fit is warmer; interaction sensitivities have the required sign and substantial magnitude. The domain mismatch is established, but an erroneous coefficient or a unique temperature-transfer mechanism is not. |
| 2 | The 2B association representation inadequately describes cyclic acid dimers and competing cross association | Ordinary vapour association exists, while a separate cyclic-dimer contribution is absent. Primary literature supports the hypothesis. The current data do not separate association error from dispersion compensation. The square/cube discrepancy is too small to explain the full excess. |
| 3 | Pure-component parameters affect the mixture error | Their negative endpoint errors partly mask the excess. Their influence through mixture nonideality remains unresolved. The rounding and inconsistent-energy controls exclude those specific substitutions only. |
| Excluded as stated | Ordinary vapour association was omitted | Nonzero association energies, bonded sites and same-state removal controls contradict this claim. |
| Excluded for the retained extraction | Component, phase-coordinate or pressure-unit transcription error | Every joined mixed row and both endpoints reproduce the raw ThermoML extraction. The original experiment and compiler uncertainty assessment remain unverified. |

A source-backed correction requires Pabsch's complete pure-parameter family,
water diameter law, association convention, vapour treatment and actual
Ito–Yoshida fitting rows and pressures.
The published coefficient must first reproduce those calibration observations.
Figure S1 alone cannot supply the complete fit inventory.
Independent acid vapour density, compressibility, second-virial or dimerization
data, together with mixture bubble and dew data over temperature, would help
separate vapour-association error from interaction transfer.
Pure saturation pressure alone cannot identify association when its parameters
were fitted to that property.

If the cause is a parameter-declaration mismatch, adopt the complete source
family and its combining rules together, then recheck pure endpoints, the
original binary calibration and this isotherm.
A different association theory or temperature-dependent interaction requires
cited equations, parameters, the source's fitting procedure and a numerical
falsifier before implementation.
An additional dimer reaction must be reconciled with the existing association
energy to avoid double counting.
No sensitivity value is proposed as a correction.

### Numerical verification and interpretation limits

{{< include results/pressure-diagnosis/verification.md >}}

The [probe results](results/pressure-diagnosis/probe-results.json) retain native
states and independent pressure and fugacity closures.
The [measurement check](results/pressure-diagnosis/measurement-check.json)
retains the raw group join, endpoints and uncertainties; pressure and pressure
uncertainty are converted together from kilopascals to pascals.
The [run identity](results/pressure-diagnosis/run-identity.json) records the
freshly built Engine source, loaded binaries and input hashes.
The [original executable identity](results/pressure-diagnosis/original-executable.json)
identifies the earlier frozen-wheel calculation.
The [pure and neutral controls](results/pressure-diagnosis/pure-neutral-controls.json)
provide a separate replay with the current installed Engine.

This is numerical reproduction and a conditional comparison with physical
measurements, without physical validation of a molecular explanation.
The decomposition uses central measured values and is deterministic bookkeeping,
not an uncertainty-complete statistical attribution.
Parameter covariance, model-form error, temperature uncertainty, experimental
covariance, the original fit implementation and full measurement treatment
remain unknown.
No unique microscopic cause or numerical implementation defect is established.

## Meaning and remaining limits

The retained evidence is **solution verification plus a conditional physical pressure comparison**.
All selected pressures are overpredicted, including after the documented composition-interval calculation.
The discrepancy is much larger than the dissociation signal and the measured pressure uncertainty.
It does not identify an Engine defect or validate speciation.
Calibration membership remains unresolved, source access limits remain explicit, and no physical-accuracy claim extends beyond this temperature and the selected states.
